title: Russian strike on ship near Odesa kills 10, Ukraine hits Moscow with drones
summary: Ukraine launches hundreds of drones towards Moscow a day after Russia unleashed a massive barrage of ballistic missiles.
full_text:
Russian strike on ship near Odesa kills 10, Ukraine hits Moscow with drones
Ukraine is hitting Moscow with drones after Russia unleashed one of its largest ballistic missile barrages at Kyiv.
A Russian strike on a ship near the southern Ukrainian port city of Odesa has killed at least 10 people, while Ukraine has launched hundreds of drones to attack Moscow, a day after Kyiv was hit by one of the heaviest barrages of ballistic missiles of the war.
Russia struck a Guinea-Bissau-flagged ship carrying corn with a crew from India and Syria, Ukraine’s seaports authority said on Monday. Officials said eight crew members had been rescued.

- list 3 of 4Ukrainian drone attacks on Russia kill at least 8, wound dozens
- list 4 of 4Russia launches largest ballistic missile attack on Kyiv since start of war
Russian strikes in Odesa have now killed 28 people in the month of July alone, regional governor Oleh Kiper said.
“Since the beginning of July, the Odesa region was under constant daily shelling. There were days when 13 to 15 air raid alerts had been announced in the region,” Kiper told Ukrainian television.
Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces had hit fuel reservoirs at Odesa’s port.
Russia has stepped up its attacks on Ukraine, frequently using ballistic missiles, as Kyiv is currently short of Patriot interceptor munitions that are crucial to defend against them.
In retaliation, Ukraine is intensifying its attacks on Russian territory. It targeted Moscow and the surrounding region with hundreds of drones overnight, wounding at least 10 people and setting several buildings ablaze, Russian officials said.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 400 “enemy drones” were launched at the Moscow region between 8:30 p.m. (17:30 GMT) and 5:00 a.m. (02:00 GMT). Most were intercepted by Russia’s air defence systems, including 85 destroyed while approaching the Russian capital.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine struck Russian logistics facilities and an oil depot in the Moscow region more than 400 km (250 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
“We are responding, justly, to every Russian strike against our cities and communities,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X.
“Overnight, air defence forces and electronic warfare systems repelled a drone attack on the Moscow region. The main consequences were recorded in Podolsk, Domodedovo, and the Odintsovo district,” Andrei Vorobyov, the governor of the Moscow region, wrote on the Telegram messaging app. He said 10 people, including a child, were wounded, and three of the wounded were Chinese citizens.
“According to preliminary information, one person was wounded in Domodedovo as a result of a fire at a private house, and another on the M-4 highway, where a drone fell near a vehicle,” Vorobyov said.
Wildberries, Russia’s largest online retailer, said on Monday its logistics centre in the Podolsk district had been evacuated as a precaution, but later resumed normal operations.This comes after a series of Ukrainian drone attacks killed at least eight warehouse workers from Wildberries on Saturday and injured dozens more, while another attack sparked a fire at an oil depot outside Moscow.
Ukrainian drones also struck seven Russian vessels on Sunday night in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov, according to Kyiv’s drone forces commander Robert Brovdi. He said that the targets included three tankers and four dry cargo ships, bringing the total number of vessels struck in July to 183. Brovdi added that seven substations had been hit in Russia-occupied Crimea.

title: Putin meets North Korean foreign minister in diplomatic push
summary: The visit by North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui comes without an obvious occasion, such as a multilateral diplomatic event or state anniversary, and has raised speculation that she may be coordinating a possible visit to Russia by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
full_text:
Putin meets North Korean foreign minister in diplomatic push
SEOUL, South Korea — Russian President Vladimir Putin met with North Korea's foreign minister and thanked Pyongyang for supporting his war against Ukraine, in the latest high-level diplomacy between the countries, Russian state media reported.
The visit by North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui comes without an obvious occasion, such as a multilateral diplomatic event or state anniversary, and has raised speculation that she may be coordinating a possible visit to Russia by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. North Korean state media said Choe departed for Russia on Saturday at the invitation of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov but has yet to comment on the purpose of her visit.
Yoon Min Ho, spokesperson for South Korea's Unification Ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, said Monday that Seoul was closely monitoring the meetings but declined to assess whether Moscow and Pyongyang were discussing another summit between their leaders.
Russia's Tass news agency said Putin during his meeting with Choe at the Kremlin on Sunday praised the countries' bilateral relations and reiterated his "gratitude to the North Korean leadership and people" for supporting his military operations against Ukraine. Choe told Putin that Kim remains committed to the "comprehensive development" of relations with Russia, Tass said.
Kim traveled to Russia's Far East for summits with Putin in 2019 and 2023. Putin invited Kim to visit Russia again during their summit in Pyongyang in June 2024, where the leaders signed a strategic partnership agreement pledging mutual aid if either country faces aggression.
Kim in recent years has made Russia the priority of his foreign policy, sending thousands of troops and huge supplies of weapons to support Putin's war in Ukraine, possibly in exchange for economic aid and technology transfers that some experts say are helping advance North Korea's military capabilities.
Kim has also been seeking stronger ties with China, including hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping for a June summit in Pyongyang, as he embraces the idea of a "new Cold War" and projecting Pyongyang as part of a united front against Washington.
Choe's visit to Moscow came shortly after North Korea and China exchanged high-level visits, with North Korean Cabinet premier, Pak Thae Song, Kim's top economic official, meeting Xi in Beijing and Wang Huning, a member of the Chinese Communist Party's powerful Politburo Standing Committee, visiting Kim in Pyongyang this month.
Kim has suspended all meaningful dialogue with the United States and South Korea since the collapse of his nuclear diplomacy with U.S. President Donald Trump in 2019. He has used Russia's war on Ukraine as a distraction to accelerate the advancement of his nuclear weapons and missile program, while demanding that Washington abandon its calls for North Korea's nuclear disarmament as a precondition for talks.

Finbarr Berminghamin Brussels
As trade tensions with China reach boiling point, EU officials are ramping up engagement with Beijing in search of an off-ramp.
Quietly behind the scenes, though, Europe is preparing for a trade war. In Brussels, a steely determination has set in to ensure the bloc’s manufacturing heartlands are not deindustrialised by the “China Shock 2.0”.
With some industries already haemorrhaging jobs, the EU’s resilience-building and de-risking plans are now laced with deterrents as Brussels looks to acquire leverage and credible retaliatory tools that would allow it to respond if China uses trade coercively.
Some analysts say the sides are already in a trade war, others think the two sides are still preparing for the inevitable storm – and some say that a trade war should be avoided at all costs.
But a question that is increasingly being asked is: could Europe actually win?
Few in Brussels share the hubris of US President Donald Trump, who in March 2018 said “trade wars are good, and easy to win”.
During a parliamentary hearing last week, the EU’s top trade enforcer, Denis Redonnet, said the purpose of engaging with Beijing was “to avoid sleepwalking at two levels”.

title: Australian ski resorts smash July climate records with temperatures 12C above average
summary:
Resorts in NSW and Victoria face a warm and dry start to the season with only sporadic falls of natural snow in many alpine areas

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Alpine ski resorts in New South Wales and Victoria saw climate records shattered at the weekend with maximum temperatures up to 12C above average.

Ski areas of Mount Hotham and Falls Creek set July records for their hottest daytime and night-time temperatures and Thredbo also set a new hottest July day, according to the Bureau of Meteorology.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Alpine ski resorts in New South Wales and Victoria saw climate records shattered at the weekend with maximum temperatures up to 12C above average.
Ski areas of Mount Hotham and Falls Creek set July records for their hottest daytime and night-time temperatures and Thredbo also set a new hottest July day, according to the Bureau of Meteorology.
The records come after a challenging start for Australia’s ski season with dry and warm temperatures seeing only sporadic falls of natural snow in many alpine areas, leaving resorts to rely mostly on snow-making technology.
The El Niño now in place in the tropical Pacific and the bureau’s long-range forecast both pointed to generally drier and warmer conditions for alpine regions this winter – a “bad combination” for snow.
Climate scientists have long warned that global heating will create difficult conditions for Australia’s ski resorts.
Angus Hines, a senior forecaster at the bureau, said a slow-moving high pressure system – characterised by clear skies and descending dry air – had been a key to the spiking temperatures.
He said this had also caused a “temperature inversion” where it was cooler closer to sea level than it was at higher altitudes.
“These temperatures were a substantial departure from the norm and even from previous bursts of heat for July,” he said.
“This highlights the likely issues we will have with ski seasons into the future with a warming climate.”
He said warmer than usual temperatures would remain in ski areas until about Wednesday and there was a chance of a snow flurry at the weekend, before temperatures were expected to climb early next week.
At Mount Hotham in Victoria’s alpine country, where the official temperature record goes back 36 years, the hottest July day was 8.7C in 1994.
But that record has been broken three times this month. The mercury peaked at a record 12C on Sunday in a month when the average daily maximum temperature is zero.
At Falls Creek, the highest July temperature had been 9.8C recorded in 1992. But this was eclipsed with 11.5C recorded on Saturday and then 13C reached on Sunday. The average daily maximum for July is 1.2C.
Also setting new daily temperature records in alpine regions this weekend were Thredbo (14C), Cabramurra (14.3C) and Mount William (15.2C).
Record warm night-time temperatures were also set in Mount Buller (5.7C), Mount Baw Baw (12C), Mount William (9.4C), Mount Hotham (4.6C) and Falls Creek (also 4.6C).
Dr Andrew Watkins, a climate scientist at the Climate Council, skied at Mount Hotham on Friday when temperatures were already threatening the previous 1994 record.
“It was incredibly warm up there,” he said.
“You do not expect to see temperature records that are more than 30 years old being broken by two or three degrees. It is quite phenomenal.
“I don’t think any climatologist is surprised by events like this any more. It is shocking in its own way.”
Laura Gray, from Bright in Victoria, skied Mount Hotham and Falls Creek on the weekend and said she saw people skiing in T-shirts and without gloves.
“It did feel pretty bizarre and I had to keep reminding myself that it was still mid-July and not the spring,” she said.
“In the morning it was lovely to ski but once the sun got high enough on the slopes it turned slushy very quickly.”
She said the ski season, which officially started in early June around the King’s birthday long weekend, had been “pretty grim” so far.
“It is not unusual not to ski on opening weekend, but it’s been pretty dire – just pretty dry and warm. Without snow-making, we absolutely would not have been skiing at all.
“When we heard there was going to be an El Niño, that put us on edge, but I don’t think anyone could have expected these July temperatures.”
The Guardian has approached Snow Resorts Australia for comment.

title: Manufacturing union says Australia’s tax system is ‘rigged’ in bold manifesto ahead of Labor conference
summary:
AMWU calls for wealth and inheritance taxes, free education and more revenue from gas companies as it outlines ‘working-class agenda’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A new tax rate for the highest income earners, introducing wealth and inheritance taxes and extracting more revenue from gas companies form part of a new leftwing manifesto circulating ahead of the Labor party’s national conference.

The extra tax revenue could help raise the jobseeker rate, make education – including university – free, and nationalise aged care under what the Australian Manufacturing Workers’ Union (AMWU) calls a blueprint for a “working-class agenda”.

Continue reading...
full_text:
A new tax rate for the highest income earners, introducing wealth and inheritance taxes and extracting more revenue from gas companies form part of a new leftwing manifesto circulating ahead of the Labor party’s national conference.
The extra tax revenue could help raise the jobseeker rate, make education – including university – free, and nationalise aged care under what the Australian Manufacturing Workers’ Union (AMWU) calls a blueprint for a “working-class agenda”.
The AMWU describes the 32-page manifesto not as a “polite request” but a “working-class instruction to the government on how to build a society that actually works for us all”.
The union’s agenda has not been costed and goes well beyond what the Albanese government would realistically consider adopting.
But the suite of ideas will help frame the backdrop to Labor’s national conference in Adelaide this week, where MPs, trade unions and rank-and-file members will gather to thrash out the party’s policy platform.
The union for manufacturing workers is one of the loudest progressive voices in the labour movement, strongly advocating for policies such as winding-back property investor tax concessions well before the Albanese government eventually pursued it.
The new “blueprint for action” proposes a wide-ranging economic and social policies aimed at putting wealth and power into the hands of working-class people.
Describing the taxation system as “rigged in favour of private wealth accumulation and speculation”, the document suggests a new marginal tax rate for people earning above $500,000 a year.
The highest marginal tax rate is currently set at 47% – including the 2% Medicare levy – and applies to income above $190,000.
The document advocates for an annual wealth tax on assets (excluding the family home) and an inheritance tax on large bequests to prevent the “intergenerational concentration” of wealth.
The blueprint renews the AMWU’s support for higher taxes on gas exports, calling for a “fundamental reform” to the petroleum resource rent tax.
Labor is set to make an in-principle commitment to the policy at the national conference, with the text of the draft platform binding the party to ensure that taxpayers receive a “fairer return” on natural resources.
The parliamentary party is not required to implement the policy and Anthony Albanese is not considering a gas tax due to the uncertainty that the Middle East crisis has caused to the international oil market.
But entrenching the position in Labor policy would add to the pressure on the government to act, which has been building for months via a campaign from advocates including ACT senator David Pocock and the Australia Institute thinktank.
The AMWU’s blueprint also supports winding back fuel tax credits for large mining companies, which will also be up for debate at the conference.
The union’s agenda proposes adding dental to Medicare and making all levels of education, from childcare to university, free.
It also advocates raising welfare payments to end poverty and nationalising the aged care system to ensue that social security is a “right, not a precarious privilege”.
The AMWU wants workers to have veto rights over the use of artificial intelligence in their workplaces and the ability to negotiate for a share of the extra revenue it might generate.
The blueprint also proposes a pathway to “sovereignty and justice” for Indigenous Australians, which includes enacting the Uluru statement from the heart – including the voice to parliament – and abolishing symbols of “colonial oppression”, such as the union jack on the Australia flag, from public life.
The union declined to comment on the blueprint or clarify if it intended to specifically push the various ideas at Labor national conference, which runs from Thursday to Saturday.

title: At-home STI test pulled from Australian shelves after failing to detect infections
summary:
Exclusive: TGA finds Touch Biotechnology test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea ‘is not reliable’ and has affected an unspecified number of people

Australia’s only approved home test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea has been pulled from shelves after it failed to detect infections for an unspecified number of patients.

full_text:
Australia’s only approved home test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea has been pulled from shelves after it failed to detect infections for an unspecified number of patients.
Touch Biotechnology has been handed a six‑month suspension by the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) after a review of the company’s self‑testing kit found “the device is not reliable … and poses a high risk for false negative results for users”.
The product first hit pharmacy shelves in December 2024, with a typical retail price of $24. The STI test involves taking a vaginal swab that is then placed in a container with testing solution.
During its review of the product, the TGA said it was also alerted by a health service in May about “false negative results from this test, affecting an unspecified number of patients”. The TGA could not reveal which health service raised the concern.
The regulator said it “does not have a reliable estimate of how many users may have received false negative results”.
Touch Biotechnology’s general manager, Mazz Gencer, said the company “acknowledges the TGA’s action and has ceased supply” of the tests as “further verification and performance testing are completed”.
At the time of approval, the company said its product correctly identified more than 99% of positive cases for both chlamydia and gonorrhoea when compared against urine PCR testing, and did not produce any false positives.
Touch Biotechnology said it had followed “the established regulatory assessment process applicable at the time of registration” to support its claimed limit of detection and overall performance, but declined to share any evidence, saying it was “not disclosing non-public regulatory submissions, documents or technical information”.
As part of the conditions of approval two years ago, Touch Biotechnology was required to maintain a post‑market surveillance report, including information on any adverse events, such as any reported false positive or false negative results.
The company declined to provide findings of any reviews, saying it is “not disclosing non-public post-market surveillance records or technical reports”.
When the product was approved by the TGA in late 2024, sexual health experts urged caution, including the deputy medical director at Sexual Health Victoria, Dr Sara Whitburn.
Whitburn said the TGA’s findings “highlight the need for stronger evidence requirements and ongoing oversight of self-testing kits” and called for stronger “independent evidence, including peer-reviewed clinical data and real-world performance studies” before further future approvals of similar products.
She warned that false negatives can have serious consequences for individuals and their partners.
“As chlamydia and gonorrhoea are often asymptomatic, an undetected infection can remain untreated and be passed on to sexual partners. For some people, delayed diagnosis and treatment can lead to complications such as pelvic inflammatory disease, infertility and ectopic pregnancy,” Whitburn said.
Whitburn said “at-home STI self-tests can play an important role in making testing more accessible … they shouldn’t replace clinic-based care”, but stressed “a negative result doesn’t always rule out an STI”.
“In my view, at-home STI self-tests are a valuable option to support people to consider their sexual health and seek out testing for STI, but they work best as part of the broader healthcare system,” Whitburn said.
“If you used this self-test and received a negative result, you should see a doctor or visit a sexual health clinic for further assessment and have a laboratory test to confirm your result.”

Italy condemns Russia's move to expel military attache from Moscow 'without cause'
Meanwhile, Italy’s foreign minister Antonio Tajani said that Russia had expelled an Italian military attache and one of his aides from Moscow “without cause,” AFP reported.
Tajani wrote on X that it represented a “blatant act of retaliation for Italy’s expulsion of two Russian military attachés”, whom he said had been caught spying against Rome.
Hungary opens probe into Chinese BYD carmaker's investment in country negotiated by previous government
Separately, Hungary’s government announced an investigation Monday into a large foreign investment by Chinese automaker BYD negotiated by a former foreign minister who last week resigned from parliament to take an executive position at the company, AP reported.
Péter Szijjártó’s announcement last Wednesday that he would take the job at the world’s top electric carmaker prompted accusations of a conflict of interest and criticism over his role in facilitating substantial government subsidies to the company while in office.
Prime minister Péter Magyar told lawmakers on Monday that Szijjártó, a close ally of former prime minister Viktor Orbán, had helped BYD while he was in office “with hundreds of billions (of forints) in public money, diplomatic support and state infrastructure.”
“We will examine all the decisions, negotiations and state commitments made by Péter Szijjártó that were related to the BYD Hungary investment,” Magyar said..
He added the investigation would look into all subsidies, tax breaks, permits, environmental exemptions and publicly funded investments given to large multinational firms during Orbán’s tenure, AP said.
Hungary’s Magyar picks chess prodigy for president after ousting Orbán-era loyalist
Ashifa Kassam
European community affairs correspondent
In other news, Hungary’s prime minister, Péter Magyar, has announced plans to ask Judit Polgár, widely considered the greatest female chess player of all time, to take on the largely ceremonial role of president.
Magyar said he would meet Polgár on Monday to discuss the matter. “Our country needs unity, peace and a president that all Hungarians can be proud of,” he wrote on social media. “Judit Polgár’s name has been synonymous with talent and perseverance for decades.”
The announcement by Magyar follows a months-long standoff between the newly elected leader and Tamás Sulyok, the president appointed during former leader Viktor Orbán’s time in power.
Since his landslide victory in April, Magyar has repeatedly called on Sulyok to step down, accusing him of being an Orbán “puppet” who had failed to stand up for the country as Orbán’s rightwing, nationalist Fidesz party was criticised for weakening democratic institutions and undermining the rule of law.
Last week Hungary’s parliament – where Magyar’s Tisza party holds a two-thirds majority – voted to back a constitutional amendment that included an immediate end to Sulyok’s term.

Luke Harding
in Kyiv
Ukraine’s top military leadership has denied reports that the country’s commander in chief Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi is to be sacked.
In a Facebook post published in the last few minutes it said claims “circulating in the media, particularly on social media and in certain news outlets are untrue”.
It added:
“Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi continues to carry out his duties as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.The Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, Lt Gen Andriy Hnatov, also continues to carry out his duties.
Dismissal from these posts takes place on the basis of a decree by the President of Ukraine.”
Zelenskyy’s presidential adviser Dmytro Lytvyn appeared to confirm the denial.
“Don’t expect any personnel appointments today,” he said, urging people to treat information circulated by the media with caution.
“Congratulations to Andy Burnham @andyburnham on taking office as prime minister of the United Kingdom. We wish the prime minister and the British people every success in addressing the challenges of today.
Britain has always been one of the global leaders. We are ready to work together in all possible formats. We highly appreciate the UK’s political, defense, and values-based support. The foundation of our bilateral relationship is stronger than ever, and we will continue to make each other stronger. I’m looking forward to our conversation later today. Thank you!”
Pressure on Ukraine's army chief Syrskyi grows after days of street protests
Luke Harding
in Kyiv
Meanwhile, Ukrainian media are reporting that Ukraine’s Commander in Chief, Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi is to be sacked, following five days of noisy street protests calling for his dismissal.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy has reportedly agreed to fire Syrskyi after controversially sacking defence minister Mykhailo Federov last week.
Thousands of demonstrators gathered outside Zelenskyy’s office, calling for Federov’s reinstatement and for the commander in chief’s removal.
The news has not been confirmed, but sources indicate an announcement is expected this afternoon. There is speculation Federov will be brought back into government as deputy prime minister for military industry.
Federov is widely credited with improving Ukraine’s position on the battlefield during his six months in the job. He accused Syrskyi of using Soviet era tactics and allocating resources to brigades based on their “loyalty” rather than data.
“This sort of culture needs to be eradicated, because otherwise we won’t be able to defeat an enemy whose system is plagued by the very same issues,” he said. “We have no other choice if we want to defeat Russia asymmetrically, with minimal losses.”

title: The Biggest Hygiene Mistakes People Make in the Pool
summary: Chlorine is great. It's just not magic.
full_text:
On a 95°F day, when you’re drenched with sweat and desperate to cool down, a swimming pool might look like the most beautiful thing you’ve ever seen. But to the people who study pool water for a living, it’s more like a warm, lightly chlorinated broth of everything a few dozen bodies carried in with them. That's not a reason to stay on dry land—but it
a reason to know the handful of habits that can tip a day at the pool from refreshing to regrettable.
We asked infectious disease doctors and water-quality experts which hygiene mistakes they see most. Here's what you're probably getting wrong—and what to do instead.
You think chlorine zaps everything the second it hits the water
Chlorine is a genuinely great disinfectant, but it doesn't work instantly, and it's not all-powerful.
Ordinary bacteria don't stand a chance: "Chlorine, when it comes into direct contact with bacteria, in less than a minute, that bacteria dies," says Kelly Reynolds, an environmental microbiologist at the University of Arizona who studies how pathogens spread. But a virus like hepatitis, which can be contracted through water, can take about 15 minutes. And the
single most common cause of pool outbreaks
in the U.S.—can live in chlorinated water for roughly 10 days. To kill it, operators have to "shock" a pool with around 20 times the usual chlorine, and even that takes hours. Most of the time, though,
is removed gradually as the pool's filtration system continuously circulates and filters the water.
In other words, a swimming pool isn’t one giant bottle of Purell. Reynolds has watched people wipe a kid's nose or change a diaper and then rinse their hands in the pool, figuring the chlorine will handle it. "They think of pool water as a sanitizing liquid, and it's not," she says—a pool runs around one part chlorine per million parts water, while hand sanitizer is about 60% alcohol.
That's also why you don't want to swallow any of it: You wouldn't gulp bathwater after a few other people had been soaking in it, Reynolds says.
You skip the pre-swim rinse
Almost nobody showers before getting into the pool, which is a shame, because it's one of the easiest ways to make the water cleaner for everyone. A quick rinse knocks off sweat, sunscreen, body oils, and—let's be honest—the traces you carry from the bathroom, so you're not dumping that load into the shared water or feeding the germs already in it.
"If you shower before, you could help keep the pool cleaner," says Lisa Cuchara, a professor of biomedical sciences at Quinnipiac University who teaches a course called “The Infections of Leisure,” about the germs people encounter while swimming, traveling, camping, spending the day at the spa, and pursuing other recreational activities.
But, "if you shower after, you could help prevent yourself from coming down with something," she adds. A second shower washes away whatever was floating in the water, as well as the chlorine that can dry out your skin and hair.
Neither one has to be elaborate. If your pool has one of those little rinse-off showers by the deck, 30 seconds before you get in—and another quick rinse when you get out—goes a long way.
You get in with an open cut, scrape, or fresh surgical site
Your skin is a remarkably good barrier—right up until there's a break in it. Chlorine doesn't magically seal a shaving nick, scraped knee, or healing surgical incision.
"When people have open wounds and then they go into the pool, they're exposing their body to a lot of potential pathogens," says Dr. Daniel Egan, an infectious disease specialist at Orlando Health. "It's true that chlorine reduces risk of infection in these pools, but it never sets it to zero."
How much that matters depends on the wound. A small cut isn't much of an issue, Egan says; a large abrasion or a surgical site is—and the risk climbs in untreated water like a lake or the ocean. "Ideally you don't want to jump into a pool when you have an open wound," he says. "But if you do, change the dressing. Make sure it's dry."
That means sealing it with a waterproof dressing (such as Tegaderm), rather than a standard bandage, before you get in. Once you're out of the pool, pat the skin dry and replace it with a fresh dressing. And if you've recently had surgery, don't assume you're ready to swim just because the stitches are out. Your skin may still be healing, so get clearance from your doctor before jumping in.
You never wash your feet
"Don't get me started on feet," says Dr. Alok Vij, director of dermatologic surgery at Vitalogy Skincare in Austin. Then he gets started on feet: They’re “one of the body's highest-bacteria zones," he says, along with the face, underarms, groin, and hands. Which makes it all the more alarming that “most people don’t wash their feet, period,” he says.
the more often people lather up their feet with soap, the fewer bacteria they tend to carry there. Going from washing once a day to twice a day drops the bacterial load on your skin dramatically. One of those bacteria is
, which also thrives in under-sanitized pools and happens to cause swimmer's ear. In other words, that classic summer ear infection may have started on someone's foot.
So give your feet actual attention in the shower—especially before you swim—instead of assuming the water running over them counts as washing. This is especially important if you're coming from the beach: Sand clogs a pool's filters, and a pool that can't filter can't clean itself.
Most people file this one under gross-but-harmless. Yet peeing in the pool is actually “really bad," Cuchara says.
The reason is chemistry, not germs. Urine reacts with the chlorine that's supposed to be killing germs and uses it up, producing chloramine: that unmistakable "pool smell" many people mistake for cleanliness. Every bathroom break you skip makes the disinfectant weaker for everyone else.
That’s why the ocean gets a pass. "The urine itself isn't the problem," Cuchara says. There's no chlorine out there to sabotage, and the volume is, well, the ocean. "The whales are peeing in the ocean," she points out.
In a pool, there's no way around it: Get out and use the bathroom.
You marinate in a wet bathing suit
The instinct to lounge around in a damp suit all afternoon is working against your skin. Waterlogged skin is more permeable, and a wet suit keeps it that way. "It's like a party of fungus, yeast, bacteria, and viral agents," says Dr. Kimberly Eickhorst of Dermatology Associates of Western CT—all of which love a warm, damp, dark environment and are happy to set up camp when your skin barrier is softened.
She commonly sees “hot tub folliculitis,” an itchy, pimply rash caused by
bacteria that thrives in hot tubs. Patients arrive baffled, and her first question—"Have you been in a hot tub?"—often cracks the case.
Change out of your wet swimsuit as soon as you're done swimming, then take a quick shower. You'll wash away chlorine, help restore your skin's natural pH, and make it a lot harder for unwanted microbes to settle in.
You assume your swimsuit cleans itself
Just because it spent all day in the water doesn't mean it's clean. Your suit is still carrying your skin cells, body oils, sunscreen, and whatever else was floating around in the pool.
"You wash your underwear every time you wear it," Vij points out, and you should treat your swimsuit the same way.
Left unwashed, a swimsuit becomes a breeding ground for fungus and bacteria. At minimum, rinse it thoroughly in clean water before letting it dry, which also helps flush out chlorine and sunscreen that can damage the fabric; using detergent does an even more thorough job.
You let your ears drip dry
"A pocket of still water sitting in the ear canal is a recipe for disaster," Egan says. There are always microbes living on your skin, and trapped moisture gives them exactly the environment they need to multiply.

title: Dr. Jill Lepore on why AI backlash is vital for the future
summary: Today, I’m talking with Harvard professor and New Yorker staff writer Dr. Jill Lepore about her new book, The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State, which comes out on August 25. Jill is one of the best writers there is at identifying institutional patterns in history, and Decoder is a show about systems, so […]
full_text:
Today, I’m talking with Harvard professor and New Yorker staff writer Dr. Jill Lepore about her new book, The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State, which comes out on August 25.
Dr. Jill Lepore on why AI backlash is vital for the future
The Artificial State author explains how counting everything breaks society — and how college grads booing AI might save us all.
Jill is one of the best writers there is at identifying institutional patterns in history, and Decoder is a show about systems, so this book could not possibly be more in our zone.
You build systems by measuring things — gathering information, quantifying it as data, and taking action on it. And Jill’s big thesis in the book is that this kind of systemic measurement is really a dehumanizing act, one that flattens human concerns into something, well, artificial.
These artificial structures touch everything — not just in the more obvious places like in apps or AI, but all the way up to politics and governance itself, and Jill’s insights here are a telling portrait of the way Big Tech and its billionaire figureheads have managed to break the very idea of the state itself.
Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here. Not a subscriber? You can sign up here.
You’ll hear Jill tell me she wanted to write a “kind of grumpy book,” but in my reading, it’s a pretty dead-ahead look at the last century and a half of technological and social developments and how we got to a place where bots are maybe running everything.
Jill’s idea of the artificial state starts with the very idea of quantification, from the first stabs at taking a census thousands of years ago to the invention of modern political polling in the 1930s. But where she really sees a big pivot — and the era she and I talked about most — is in the 1980s, when we saw the emergence of the Silicon Valley culture we have today, when computers got personal, and when computer-aided targeting and microtargeting really truly became both possible and commonplace, both for ads and for political campaigns.
What Jill and I did disagree about is some of her pessimism about the internet, because the internet is what made jobs and careers like mine — and businesses like The Verge, and shows like Decoder — even possible at all. There really was a great democratizing of access that happened in the late 20th century and into the 21st, as people got online, and not all of it was as illusory as maybe the great hopes for Twitter after the Arab Spring turned out to be.
But as I said, Jill thinks in systems, and so her response, about the way systems of power keep adapting to how people use new technology, was as illuminating as ever.
Of course, we also talked about the future — including where she thinks she still sees hope for the future. And yes, that does include college kids booing the AI CEOs at graduation ceremonies.
Okay: Dr Jill Lepore, on the Artificial State. Here we go.
This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.
Dr. Jill Lepore, you’re a staff writer at The New Yorker, you’re a professor of history and law at Harvard University, and most importantly, you’re the author of a new book, The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State. Welcome to Decoder.
Hey, thanks for having me.
I am really excited to talk to you. I’m a big fan of your work over the years. And I have to say, this book is one of the most Decoder-y, Verge-y, Nilay-Patel-strike-zone books of all time.
[Laughs] Wow. I’m not sure how to take that, but I guess that’s good.
The producers and I just had a thrill ride reading this book. It is essentially about how computers and measurement flatten us and then systems can take advantage of that flattening. Like I said, it’s in the strike zone.
So let’s just start at the very beginning for folks. The book is called The Rise and Fall of the Artificial State. Tell us what the “artificial state” is. Define it so we can start from that foundation.
What I mean by the artificial state is a successor to the liberal nation-state, the constitutional democracy under which our freedom of speech, free discourse, and constitutional rights are central to our experience as citizens within a nation-state.
We talk a lot about democratic decay and democratic backsliding, and there’s a whole public discussion of what’s happening with democracy, but I don’t think we talk about the nation-state as much as we might. And that is to say the state itself.
And so what I mean by the ‘artificial state’ is a state in which more and more of the functions of the nation-state have been taken over by private multinational corporations. The easiest example of that to think about is what is euphemistically called the public square, which is where people get information about how to vote, what’s going on in the world, how to make decisions, and how to exercise their rights and duties as citizens.
Our public discourse is almost entirely privatized and owned by corporations. As many, many people have demonstrated — it’s not news to your listeners or to anyone — the priority of public discourse is not the free expression of ideas and democratic deliberation, it is the monetization of attention and of outrage.
More than that, a fairly recent vintage is the fact that public platforms in which we exchange ideas as citizens and democracies are dominated by bots. All of them have been inverted for several years now, or different numbers of years, from X to Facebook to TikTok. There are far more bots than humans on those platforms.
Many of those bots are owned by corporations and have particular acts, their own kind of financial interests, but they’re owned by state actors, non-state actors, criminals, and terrorists. What we’re at risk of is losing the liberal constitutional democracy and having it become supplanted by what I describe as the artificial state.
One of the things that really struck me about this is at least America’s conception of itself, the United States’ conception of itself is this messy, multi-part democracy. The Senate loves to call itself the most deliberative body in the history of the world, and it’s supposed to be a whole bunch of people that are ruled by the consent of the governed and we’re all arguing.
Your thesis is that that’s what we say about ourselves, but actually we’ve automated away and numerically quantified away a bunch of that, and we are now run maybe by bots on Twitter, or at least politicians are overwhelmed by bots on Twitter and they’ve outsourced their thinking, or there are consultants that are turning us all into polling data. Is that the trajectory we’re on that ends the nation-state? Is that the core of the idea?
Yeah. It has a long history, but the acceleration of these developments in the age of artificial intelligence is really considerable. I’ll give you two examples that stretch out across a century. In the 1930s, we see the invention of so-called scientific polling. George Gallup starts the American Institute of Public Opinion research in 1935.
What polling does gradually over the middle decades of the 20th century is replace the kind of door-to-door precinct walking that campaigns would need to do, right? If I’m running for election in some neighborhood, I have to go talk to people. I’m going to go to baseball games, basketball games, and the public library. But increasingly, it became less necessary for political campaigns to do that because they could subcontract out political polling.
You can find out what political opinion is in a neighborhood if you want to run a campaign just by doing data mining and data analysis.
We might say, “That makes politics so much more efficient. Those campaigns can more efficiently use their money and they can get their message out to the right people.” But if you think about each one of those conversations that people used to have — “I’m a campaign volunteer and I’m going to go and I’m going to sit in on some PTA mee

title: The AirPods Max 2 are down to their second-best price
summary: There are a ton of deals available to shop today thanks to Best Buy’s “Black Friday in July” sale lasting all week. The sale typically aligns closely with Prime Day each year, but of course, Amazon’s shopping holiday happened much earlier than we expected. So it’s nice to have some deals in July. One of […]
full_text:
There are a ton of deals available to shop today thanks to Best Buy’s “Black Friday in July” sale lasting all week. The sale typically aligns closely with Prime Day each year, but of course, Amazon’s shopping holiday happened much earlier than we expected. So it’s nice to have some deals in July.
The AirPods Max 2 are down to their second-best price
A great price if you missed out on the $150 off Prime Day sale. Logitech’s haptics-based gaming mouse is also discounted.
A great price if you missed out on the $150 off Prime Day sale. Logitech’s haptics-based gaming mouse is also discounted.
One of example of a great deal is Apple’s AirPods Max 2, which are down to $449.99 at Amazon and Best Buy, $100 off their usual price. It’s only the second time they’ve been discounted. Prime Day knocked them all the way down to $399.99, but today’s price isn’t bad at all if you missed out last month. They’re available at this price in every color.
Our review called the Max 2 a “great sequel, but not an ambitious one.” In short, not much has changed, especially in terms of design. There are some internal improvements that might make it worth it for those who have the original iteration (especially if you have the model with the Lightning connector). The Max 2 features USB-C connectivity like the 2024 revision, but has a built-in amp that delivers incredible sound that edges out the competition, not to mention the H2 wireless chip that enables features like live translation, adaptive audio, and conversation awareness.
Some other great Verge-approved deals
- The Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike wireless gaming mouse is a fascinating PC gaming accessory. Instead of having physical switches under its two main mouse buttons, it uses haptic motors to simulate the click sensation. The company made the switch to decrease latency, and to let you customize how much of a jolt each click delivers. If that sounds interesting to you, read our coverage, and consider picking it up at its first-ever discount at Amazon. The $179.99 mouse is down to $125.99, a temporary price cut that’ll be reflected at the checkout screen.
- Some other great Apple deals switched on overnight, including a four-pack of AirTags (second-gen) Bluetooth trackers. Originally $99.99, the four-pack is down to $89.99 at Amazon and Best Buy. Costco members can get an even better deal with five second-gen AirTags for $99.99. The latest AirTags’ biggest features include a louder alarm and extended range, which could give you a better chance at finding your lost items compared to the first-gen version, even if it’s four floors below (something the original AirTag couldn’t reliably do). Read Victoria Song’s review.
- Kodak’s Charmera isn’t a great camera. Let’s get that out of the way first. However, the name is on point — it’s charming as heck. The quality of the photos isn’t what you should buy it for. It’s just fun to have a flash-ready, screen-equipped digital camera connected to your keychain. Each Charmera comes in a blind box, so you won’t know which design you’ll get until you open it. If that sounds thrilling, you can try it out yourself with a good discount from Best Buy, where it costs $33.49 through the day (originally $49.99).

title: Electric air taxis go to war
summary: Electric aviation is still in its infancy, but manufacturers are already looking beyond mere air taxi trips across cities. Today, one of the leading air taxi startups, San Jose-based Archer Aviation, unveiled a new aircraft it co-developed with defense technology company Anduril - though the platform is designed for both military and commercial uses, the […]
full_text:
Electric aviation is still in its infancy, but manufacturers are already looking beyond mere air taxi trips across cities. Today, one of the leading air taxi startups, San Jose-based Archer Aviation, unveiled a new aircraft it co-developed with defense technology company Anduril — though the platform is designed for both military and commercial uses, the companies said.
Electric air taxis go to war
Archer Aviation revealed the Thunder hybrid vertical takeoff and landing aircraft that it co-developed with Palmer Luckey’s Anduril.
Archer Aviation revealed the Thunder hybrid vertical takeoff and landing aircraft that it co-developed with Palmer Luckey’s Anduril.
The new aircraft looks like a cross between Archer’s Midnight air taxi and a more established military vertical takeoff and landing aircraft like a V-22 Osprey. Anduril, which was founded by Palmer Luckey, unveiled the new variant, called Thunder, on Monday at the Farnborough International Airshow in Hampshire, England. It’s intended to be a fully autonomous attack rotorcraft that flies alongside military crewed aircraft. Archer says it plans on unveiling a commercial version later this week.
Thunder differs from Midnight in that it’s a series hybrid powertrain, as opposed to a fully electric one. The hybrid system will help the aircraft achieve significantly longer range “while still maintaining the necessary precision to closely optimize power through the full range of flight conditions,” Archer says. Air taxi companies are increasingly turning to hybrid power to expand beyond air taxi applications and tap into broader markets. Archer said it foresees Thunder being used in military strikes, cargo shipment, remote logistics, and other operations in hard-to-reach locations.
Air taxi companies are also looking to military partnerships to help stem their enormous losses. Air taxis have yet to obtain the necessary approvals in most markets that would allow them to launch their commercial service and bring in more money. Archer lost $217.7 million in the first quarter of 2026, having generated only $1.6 million in revenue. Archer has said it intends to launch its air taxi service as soon as 2026, with the first market likely to be Abu Dhabi.
Archer has already signaled its interest in branching out into military and defense programs. Last year, the air taxi company said it would license its electric vertical and takeoff technology to Anduril, including supplying its electric powertrain and other tech to the defense contractor’s Omen drone program. Archer has also delivered one of its Midnight eVTOL aircraft to the US Air Force as part of its evaluation program.

title: Avengers: Doomsday’s first trailer puts everyone on high alert
summary: After months of teasing us with reminders about how large Avengers: Doomsday's cast is going to be, Marvel has finally released a proper trailer for the film. Though Robert. Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom definitely appears to be causing a lot of the chaos in Doomsday's first trailer, the movie seems like it's going to feature […]
full_text:
After months of teasing us with reminders about how large Avengers: Doomsday’s cast is going to be, Marvel has finally released a proper trailer for the film.
Avengers: Doomsday’s first trailer puts everyone on high alert
The trailer comes just a few days before Marvel makes its big presentation at San Diego Comic-Con.
The trailer comes just a few days before Marvel makes its big presentation at San Diego Comic-Con.
Though Robert. Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom definitely appears to be causing a lot of the chaos in Doomsday’s first trailer, the movie seems like it’s going to feature more than a few moments where different teams of heroes fight one another. Thor (Chris Hemsworth) seems to be the only person who understands that the X-Men, the Fantastic Four, and the (New) Avengers need to be more focused on dealing with their new Latverian enemy. And while Thor might not be able to rally the troops on his own, Steve Rogers’ (Chris Evans) presence will probably bring them all together.
The trailer makes Doomsday seem like it’s going to be another humongous spectacle that puts a lot of emphasis on our nostalgia for Marvel’s old X-Men movies. Marvel probably has a few more Doomsday details we won’t hear about until the studio comes to San Diego Comic-Con later this week, which should get people even more hyped to see the film before it hits theaters on December 18th — the same day that Dune: Part Three hits theaters.

title: Bitmine grows treasury to 5.78M ETH as Ether outpaces Bitcoin
summary: The Ethereum treasury firm added 7,430 ETH over the past week, bringing its holdings to nearly 5% of the network’s circulating supply.
full_text:
Bitmine grows treasury to 5.78M ETH as Ether outpaces Bitcoin
The Ethereum treasury firm added 7,430 ETH over the past week, bringing its holdings to nearly 5% of the network’s circulating supply.
Top Ethereum treasury company Bitmine said Monday its Ether holdings had reached 5.78 million tokens, representing about 4.8% of Ethereum’s circulating supply, as the company closed in on its stated goal of accumulating 5% of all ETH.
According to Monday’s announcement, the company added 7,430 ETH (ETH) over the past week. About 4.9 million ETH, or roughly 85% of its treasury, is currently staked through its validator network and partners.
Bitmine valued its crypto, cash and marketable securities at $11.5 billion, including 207 Bitcoin and $385 million in cash and securities. The company also repurchased 5.5 million shares during the week under its previously authorized $4 billion buyback program.
Earlier this month, BitMine said its institutional staking platform, MAVAN, generated $45.7 million in staking and validation revenue during the three-month period ended May 31, accounting for 98% of the company’s total revenue.
BitMine shares were up more than 6% in Monday afternoon trading, bringing their one-month gain to around 3.3%.
Source: Yahoo Finance
Related: Bitmine announces $74M Ether buys as chair says ‘greater chances of Clarity Act passage’
Ethereum gains momentum, Strategy builds cash
The announcement comes after the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin holder Strategy paused Bitcoin (BTC) purchases for a second straight week, instead raising capital through stock sales and growing its cash reserve to more than $3.2 billion.
Ethereum (ETH) has also outperformed Bitcoin over both the past week and month. It has gained about 6.7% over the past seven days and 10% over the past month, compared with gains of roughly 5.8% and 2.6%, respectively, for Bitcoin (BTC), according to CoinGecko data at the time of writing.
Source: CoinGecko
Robinhood Chain fuels optimism around Ethereum
Earlier this month, Robinhood launched Robinhood Chain, an Ethereum layer-2 network built on Arbitrum for tokenized stocks.
During its first two weeks, the blockchain attracted more than $141 million in bridged Ether and reignited debate over whether institutional adoption of Ethereum’s scaling networks ultimately drives demand for ETH.
Max Shannon, senior research analyst at Bitwise, told Cointelegraph Robinhood Chain reflects the “growth of the Ethereum ecosystem,” particularly among traditional financial institutions.
Whether that institutional growth ultimately strengthens ETH remains an open question. ARK Invest’s Lorenzo Valente argued Robinhood Chain supports the bullish case for ETH as the ecosystem’s monetary asset, but weakens the investment thesis that Ethereum derives significant value from layer-2 fee revenue.
Bernstein analysts on Monday raised their price target on Robinhood, to $160 from $130 per share, based on their investment thesis that the online brokerage’s next phase of growth will be driven by tokenized equities and prediction markets rather than traditional crypto trading.
The firm highlighted Robinhood Chain as its proprietary infrastructure for tokenized real-world assets, enabling the platform to build on-chain financial products without relying on third-party blockchains.
The price of ETH has climbed about 20% from roughly $1,582 on July 1, when the chain launched, to around $1,900 at the time of writing.

title: Hut 8, IREN deals lift AI-focused Bitcoin mining stocks
summary: Bitcoin miners rallied as investors cheered multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure contracts, underscoring the sector’s accelerating shift toward data centers and cloud computing.
full_text:
Hut 8, IREN deals lift AI-focused Bitcoin mining stocks
Bitcoin miners rallied as investors cheered multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure contracts, underscoring the sector’s accelerating shift toward data centers and cloud computing.
Shares of several Bitcoin mining companies surged Monday after Hut 8 and IREN announced major AI infrastructure deals, reinforcing investor optimism around miners expanding into artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.
IREN, Cipher Digital, CleanSpark, Hut 8 and MARA Holdings each gained at least 11% in early Monday trading. The rally followed Hut 8’s announcement of a 15-year, $9.8 billion lease for its AI data center campus and IREN’s disclosure of $2.8 billion in cloud services contracts with AI developers. Both companies began as Bitcoin (BTC) miners before accelerating a pivot toward AI infrastructure and cloud computing as mining economics weakened.
IREN now expects its AI cloud business to generate more than $4 billion in annual recurring revenue by the end of 2026.
The rally was reflected in The Energy Mag’s TEM AI Infrastructure Growth Index, which tracks 20 companies spanning the Bitcoin mining, neocloud and AI infrastructure sectors. The index rose 1.4% on Monday and is up more than 12% over the past week.
The performance of the TEM AI Infrastructure Growth Index. 
Source: The Energy Mag
The rally in Bitcoin mining stocks coincided with a broader recovery in technology shares, as the Nasdaq Composite Index added 0.9% by midday. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, a closely watched gauge of chipmakers powering the AI boom, climbed 2% after entering a technical bear market last week, defined as a decline of 20% or more from its recent high.
Related: Bitdeer stock jumps 14% as company expands US mining hardware production
AI pivot fuels gains, raises questions
Bitcoin mining stocks have experienced sharp volatility this year as companies contend with a weak Bitcoin mining environment while increasingly pivoting toward AI infrastructure and cloud computing. According to Blocksbridge Consulting, the AI pivot has driven a sharp re-rating across the sector, but it has also attracted greater investor scrutiny over insider stock sales.
In a recent Miner Weekly newsletter, Blocksbridge said insider sales at TeraWulf, Riot Platforms, Core Scientific and Cipher Mining have drawn investor attention. Although the transactions were executed under prearranged trading plans, they have fueled questions about whether AI-driven enthusiasm pushed share prices high enough for executives to cash out.
To be sure, the AI pivot has already required substantial investment from Bitcoin miners, with much more capital still needed. Blocksbridge estimates the industry will require another $50 billion to realize its AI ambitions, with IREN facing the largest funding gap at roughly $21.1 billion.
Related: Crypto Biz: When dollars disappear, stablecoins step in

title: Nigerian president signs order on approach to crypto regulation, taxes
summary: The West African country’s executive order established a virtual asset council and addressed the fragmentation of crypto regulation for oversight and enforcement.
full_text:
Nigerian president signs order on approach to crypto regulation, taxes
The West African country’s executive order established a virtual asset council and addressed the fragmentation of crypto regulation for oversight and enforcement.
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of Nigeria has moved to address what his office called the fragmentation of digital asset regulation.
The Nigerian president’s special adviser Bayo Onanuga said that an executive order signed on Friday would “harmonize the regulation of virtual assets, strengthen cooperation among the nation’s financial, revenue and capital markets agencies, protect citizens from fraud, and safeguard the integrity of the financial system while enabling responsible innovation.”
It also established a virtual asset council headed by some of the nation’s top financial regulators to direct related policies, and Nigeria’s tax authority will update its policies on digital assets.
“[T]he order does not create a new regulator or transfer powers between agencies,” said Onanuga. “Each institution retains its full statutory mandate and independence, and the framework coordinates their work rather than replacing it. To provide certainty for operators and protection for the public, registration will follow the nature of the activity and the asset involved [...] This closes the gaps through which unregistered operators have previously escaped oversight.“
Nigeria has seen some of the strongest growth in digital asset adoption in Africa, in both cryptocurrencies and stablecoins. According to a June report from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the country accounted for about 60% of stablecoin inflows within sub-Saharan Africa since 2019 and had about $59 billion in crypto inflows between July 2023 and June 2024.
Source: IMF
Related: Blockchain.com expands into Ghana after 700% trading surge in Nigeria
“The policy challenge is to narrow the gap that made the workaround [in cross-border payments] attractive, while ensuring that new risks remain contained,” said the IMF on Nigeria’s stablecoin adoption. “That requires a clear strategy: open to innovation but anchored in sound macroeconomic policy and effective regulation.”
Nigerian tax authority revamped digital assets approach
While the executive order said that the country’s tax authority, the Nigerian Revenue Service, would provide additional details on the effects on taxpayers, the agency had already announced policy reforms.
In January, authorities said that under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, crypto service providers were required to link transactions to tax identification numbers and, in some cases, national identification numbers.

title: Bernstein raises Robinhood price target, cites tokenization and prediction markets
summary: The brokerage’s blockchain strategy, including tokenized equities and its Arbitrum-based Robinhood Chain, could reduce its reliance on traditional crypto trading, analysts said.
full_text:
Bernstein raises Robinhood price target, cites tokenization and prediction markets
The brokerage’s blockchain strategy, including tokenized equities and its Arbitrum-based Robinhood Chain, could reduce its reliance on traditional crypto trading, analysts said.
Analysts at Bernstein have raised their price target on Robinhood Markets, based on their investment thesis that the online brokerage’s next phase of growth will be driven by tokenized equities and prediction markets rather than traditional crypto trading.
In a Monday research note, Bernstein raised its price target on Robinhood (HOOD) stock to $160 from $130 per share and maintained its Outperform rating. HOOD stock was last seen trading around $101.
The analysts said prediction markets are poised to become Robinhood’s fastest-growing business, forecasting segment revenue to reach $1.7 billion by 2028, representing a 64% compound annual growth rate.
Beyond prediction markets, Bernstein identified tokenized equities as a major long-term opportunity, pointing to Robinhood’s investment in blockchain infrastructure. The firm highlighted Robinhood Chain, the company’s Arbitrum-based layer-2 network, as its proprietary infrastructure for tokenized real-world assets, enabling the platform to build on-chain financial products without relying on third-party blockchains.
Bernstein said that tokenization is emerging as a foundational layer for capital markets, projecting that the value of onchain real-world assets will grow to between $2 trillion and $4 trillion by 2030 from roughly $35 billion today. The analysts expect tokenized equities to account for an increasing share of that growth as adoption expands beyond Treasury securities and private credit.
Robinhood is competing across key “battleground” asset classes, including prediction markets, perpetual futures and tokenized RWAs. Source: Bernstein
Related: Tradable’s $1B Stellar deal adds to institutional tokenization boom
Wall Street expands tokenization infrastructure
The Bernstein report comes as financial institutions continue to expand infrastructure for tokenized securities.
On Monday, brokerage infrastructure provider Alpaca and financial technology company Broadridge Financial Solutions announced they had integrated Broadridge’s shareholder governance tools into Alpaca’s Instant Tokenization Network. The integration adds capabilities such as proxy voting, investor communications and regulatory disclosures for tokenized securities, aiming to give token holders governance rights comparable to those of traditional shareholders.
The announcement follows last week’s partnership between tokenization platform Securitize and investment bank Cantor Fitzgerald to develop infrastructure for blockchain-based initial public offerings and follow-on equity offerings within existing US securities regulations.
The institutional push comes as tokenized stocks continue to gain traction. The asset class has grown to nearly $2 billion in market value this year, according to RWA.xyz.

title: Former NY Governor Cuomo joins OKX board, touts 24/7 tokenized trading
summary: Andrew Cuomo said OKX could help bring round-the-clock trading and more international capital into U.S. markets.
full_text:
Former NY Governor Cuomo joins OKX board, touts 24/7 tokenized trading
Quick Take
- Cuomo appeared on Fox Business to promote tokenized 24/7 stock trading as the former politician joins the board of crypto exchange OKX.
- Crypto exchange OKX hopes to expand its footprint in the U.S., where Coinbase is dominant.
We'd love your feedback.
Former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo appeared on Fox Business Monday to promote 24/7 tokenized stock trading after joining the board of crypto exchange OKX.
The crypto trading platform said Monday that Cuomo had joined its board of directors, deepening his existing ties to the exchange. Last month, OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange formed a 50-50 joint venture co-chaired by Cuomo.
"So crypto, OKX, fintech, coming together with ICE [and the] New York Stock Exchange — that is a marriage that should have happened a long time ago," Cuomo told Fox Business. "When people talk about crypto, they tend to talk about tokens, etc. That’s not how I see crypto. I see it as the financial infrastructure of the future."
OKX is one of the world’s largest crypto exchanges, although it trails global market leader Binance. Traditionally focused on international markets, OKX is seeking to expand in the U.S., where Coinbase dominates crypto trading and tokenized equities are attracting growing interest from crypto and traditional financial firms.
Describing ICE as the "quintessential traditional finance company," Cuomo seems to have confidence the partnership with OKX could play a role in growing the market for round-the-clock, onchain equities trading, including bringing more foreign capital into U.S. markets.
"Just imagine a world ... where you can trade stocks 24/7 internationally," he said. "Literally trillions of dollars internationally could be invested into the U.S. economy, into our exchanges."
Cuomo also explained how he believes tokenization could change equities trading.
"Tokenization says you can have fractional ownership. You can have a digital representation of that asset," Cuomo went on to say. "So you can buy a tenth of one stock, you can buy half of one stock, and the transactions digitally are immediate."
Onchain stock trading has increasingly become a focus across the crypto industry as digital-asset companies seek to bring U.S. stocks onchain and expand international access to American markets. Robinhood offers European customers tokens tied to hundreds of U.S. stocks and ETFs, while Backpack recently launched 24/7 trading in tokenized shares.
Cuomo’s public support for crypto dates back at least to last year, when his unsuccessful New York City mayoral campaign proposed creating a chief innovation officer responsible for advancing the city’s adoption of blockchain and artificial intelligence.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Are Green Again—Here’s Why Investors Should Zoom Out
summary: Two consecutive weeks of inflows ended the worst sustained outflow streak in Bitcoin ETF history. Here's why patience may be required from investors.
full_text:
In brief
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs posted $75.7 million in net inflows for the week ending July 17.
- This marks a second consecutive green week after eight straight weeks of outflows totaling more than $8.2 billion.
- The two-week recovery of $273.1 million covers just 3.3% of what investors pulled from the funds between mid-May and early July—June was the worst month on record for Bitcoin ETF products since their January 2024 launch.
Bitcoin ETFs have posted back-to-back positive weeks for the first time since early May.
The 13 U.S. spot Bitcoin funds pulled in $75.7 million in net inflows (money in exceeding money out) for the week ending July 17, according to SoSoValue data. That followed $197.4 million the prior week, bringing the two-week total to $273.1 million in net gains across the funds.
When inflows exceed outflows, the easiest translation is that retail traders are buying more Bitcoin than they are selling.
The big round number, $273 million, sounds meaningful until you zoom out. From mid-May through early July, these same funds bled through eight consecutive weeks of net outflows, draining more than $8.2 billion. June 2026 alone saw about $4.5 billion exit—the worst single month on record since these products launched.
The $273 million recovered so far is roughly 3.3 cents on every dollar lost.
Even within the latest green week, volatility showed up on Monday when $424.7 million left the funds in a single day—the largest one-day withdrawal since June 26—after renewed U.S.-Iran military escalation rattled markets. Investors reversed course the following four days and closed the week in the green.
Gold's ghost
Bitcoin ETFs are exchange-traded funds—stock market products that hold Bitcoin on investors' behalf, so you don't need to manage a crypto wallet yourself. When these funds debuted in early 2024, after years of SEC denials, they got off to a roaring start—fulfilling the promise of bringing in billions in fresh capital to the Bitcoin market.
More recently, however, as markets turned bearish, Bitcoin ETF investors have been heading for the exits.
Bloomberg Intelligence senior ETF analyst Eric Balchunas published a framework on July 17 that may be the most useful lens available for anyone holding Bitcoin ETFs right now. His argument: The 22-year history of gold ETFs—specifically GLD, the first gold ETF listed on a U.S. exchange—is the closest roadmap Bitcoin ETF investors have.
The parallel rests on a simple structural point. Both Bitcoin and gold are what analysts call "non-yielding stores of value"—they don't pay dividends, generate earnings, or carry government guarantees the way stocks and bonds do. Their price is driven by one thing: whether people want them, which makes both extremely sensitive to shifts in sentiment.
Bitcoin ETFs Likely to Mirror Gold's History of Triumph and Pain.. New from me on how gold ETFs' 22-year history may offer the closest roadmap yet for Bitcoin ETF investors. Both are wrappers around non-yielding stores of value that generate no cash flow, leaving investor… pic.twitter.com/3C4tZYPLCp
— Eric Balchunas (@EricBalchunas) July 17, 2026
GLD's history illustrates both extremes. The fund became so popular so fast that it briefly surpassed SPY—the largest stock market ETF in the world—to become the biggest ETF on the planet for a single day in 2011. Then it spent eight years in the doldrums trying to get back there.
Balchunas sees a "spiritual parallel" with IBIT: BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF briefly crossed $100 billion in assets last October, coinciding almost exactly with Bitcoin's all-time high above $126,000. Then the slide started. Bitcoin has since lost roughly half of its value, currently trading near $64,000.
But for long-term hodlers, a 50% crash isn’t really that bad of a crypto winter—at least not historically.
“Bitcoin ETFs may be following the same script: spectacular gains, painful drawdowns and recoveries that may test investors' patience,” Balchunas wrote.
BlackRock's IBIT has sold close to 100,000 BTC in recent months to meet redemptions, leaving it with just over 733,000 BTC under management. The cautious optimism from Balchunas: Every gold ETF cycle means the asset moons after a crash. "Two steps forward, one step back," he wrote—while flagging that the process can test patience for far longer than most investors expect.
Citigroup made the opposite bet on July 1. The bank cut its 12-month Bitcoin price target from $112,000 to $82,000 and reset its projected ETF inflows for the next year to zero—down from an earlier estimate of $10 billion—citing negative flows, stalled U.S. crypto legislation, and weakening institutional appetite.
The combined $77.7 billion in total net assets across all 13 spot Bitcoin ETFs is down from over $106 billion recorded just before the outflow streak began in mid-May.
